1396.3: Swayye in praise of the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. With a one-pointed mind may I meditate on the all-pervading Lord, untouched by Maya; by the Guru's grace may I ever sing the Lord's virtues; and, as I sing them, may my mind blossom. O True Guru, fulfil this hope of your servant. He who, by serving the True Guru, has attained the supreme state, and has meditated on the Imperishable, Unmanifest Lord: meeting him, poverty does not cling (to anyone); Kalsahar utters his praises. I utter the spotless virtues of that noble servant (of God) within whom the Name, the Amrit, has welled up. Serving the True Guru, he has found the relish of the Shabad and enshrined the Name of the Immaculate One in his heart. He delights in the Lord's Name, seeks out Gobind's virtues, longs for the Essence (the Lord), and is a pool of even-mindedness. O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥1॥
Thakur Hardas was Guru Ram Das Ji's father.
1396.4: (He is) a pool of Amrit, ever full, from which flow streams of Amrit that give the immortal state. Those Sants drink of it and bathe (in it) within their minds who have done service before (in past lives). Driving out their fear, he has given them the state of fearlessness, and by the Shabad alone he has carried them across. O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥2॥
1396.5: The True Guru's understanding is deep, his Sat Sangat is pure, and his soul is dyed deep red in (the Lord's) love. His mind is awake, the lotus (of his heart) has opened in Sahaj, and he has found the fearless, immaculate Lord in his own home (within). The compassionate True Guru has made the Lord's Name firm (in him); by its grace he has brought the five (passions: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under control. O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥3॥
1397.1: Through reflection he has come to know (the Lord) directly, and his attention is fixed on the One who has no parts; he has met the paaras (the touchstone that turns iron to gold: the Guru), and (dwells) in the home of Sahaj. By the True Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state, and with loving devotion his storehouses are full. He has erased birth and death, the fear of dying has fled, and his mind is fixed on the pool of contentment. O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥4॥
1397.2: He has found the Infinite, who fills the empty, and enshrined him within his heart; in his mind he has reflected on the Essence, the destroyer of sorrow, who awakens the soul. Ever in joy, in the Lord's love, he alone knows the taste of that love. By the True Guru's grace he enjoys (the Lord's) love in Sahaj. By (Guru) Nanak's grace and (Guru) Angad's wise understanding, Guru Amar Das made (the Lord's) command prevail. Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have attained the unshakable, immortal state. ॥5॥
Kalyuchrai is two words: Kal uchrai, Kal says. Amar here is a command (Persian amr).
1397.3: He dwells in the pool of contentment, and with his tongue he brings forth the taste of Amrit. Meeting him, peace wells up, and sin flees far away. He has obtained the ocean of peace, given (by the Guru), and on the Lord's path he does not tire. His armour of self-restraint, truth, contentment and gentle nature never breaks. The Creator has made him the True Guru, approved (by him), and the world has sounded the trumpet of his praise. Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have attained the fearless, immortal state. ॥6॥
1397.4: With the True Guru's approval he has won the world, and in his mind he has meditated on the One. Blessed, blessed is the True Guru Amar Das, who made the Name firm (in him). The treasure of the Name is (for him) the nine treasures; riddhis and siddhis are his handmaids. He has found the pool of Sahaj; he has met the imperishable, all-pervading Lord. The Name, holding to which the devotees from the very beginning have crossed over, the Guru has made firm in him. Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have obtained the priceless gift of the Lord's love. ॥7॥
1397.5: Streams of loving devotion (flow in him); his love from of old never runs dry. Through the True Guru's fathomless Shabad he drinks deep the taste of the streams of Amrit. Wisdom is his mother, contentment his father; he is absorbed in the pool of Sahaj. He is beyond birth, self-existent; by the Guru's word he has carried the world across. (One with the Lord,) unmanifest, beyond the reach of the senses and infinite, he has enshrined the Guru's Shabad in his mind. Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have found the saviour of the world. ॥8॥
1397.6: That saviour of the world, store of the nine treasures, carries his devotees across the world-ocean; the Lord's Name, a drop of Amrit, takes away the poison of the world. The tree of Sahaj has borne fruit: the Amrit fruits of divine knowledge hang on it. They are obtained by the Guru's grace; blessed are those fortunate people (who receive them). They have been liberated through the True Guru's Shabad, (they who) have found love for the Guru in their minds. Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have sounded the drum of the Shabad. ॥9॥
1398.1: Faith is his couch, Sahaj his canopy, contentment the wall of his tent, and an ever-gentle nature the armour that adorns him. Through the Guru's Shabad he has lived (the Name); the Name is his support, and he makes those around him fragrant (with it). Beyond birth, good and stainless, he dwells with the True Guru. Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, your dwelling is in the pool of Sahaj. ॥10॥
1398.2: Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, in their hearts he makes the Lord's Name dwell. Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, sin flees far from them. Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, he takes away their pride and conceit. Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, he attaches them to the Shabad and carries them across the world-ocean. Those who have found a true bond with the Guru, their birth in the world has borne fruit. O poet Kal, hasten to the refuge of the revered Guru; worldly gifts and liberation all (come) by clinging to the Guru. ॥11॥
1398.3: The True Guru has pitched a tent, and under it throngs from all the ages have gathered. Direct knowledge (of God) is its pole and the Name its prop, by which the devotees are fulfilled. Guru Nanak, Angad and Amar (Das), devotees, have merged in the Lord. O Guru Ram Das, you too have known the relish of this Raj and Jog. ॥12॥
1398.4: He alone is a Janak who has known (the Lord) and set the chariot (of his mind) in the state of unman; who has practised truth and contentment, and filled the empty pool (of the mind). The story of the immortal city (the unshakable state) cannot be told; he alone obtains it to whom (the Lord) gives it. O Guru Ram Das, this kingdom of Janak befits you alone. ॥13॥
1398.5: Whoever repeats the True Guru's Name in his mind, firmly, with attention fixed on the One: tell me, how can sorrow and sin come to such people? (The Guru) is the boat that carries across: the one on whom he casts his glance even for an instant reflects on the Shabad in his heart, and loses his lust and anger. He is the giver to all beings, who makes known the knowledge of the Unreachable; day and night he holds to meditation, and does not sleep even for a moment. Seeing him, poverty departs; one obtains that treasure, the Name, and through the Guru, by (his) knowledge, washes away the filth of evil-mindedness. Whoever repeats the True Guru's Name in his mind, firmly, with attention fixed on the One: tell me, how can sorrow and sin come to such people? ॥1॥
Jiu at the end of these lines is a word of respect, and is left unrendered.
1398.6: Through the Perfect True Guru, righteous living and good deeds are attained. He whose service the Siddhas, the Saadhs, the silent sages, gods and men beg for has fixed his single-pointed attention on the sublime Shabad. Who, moreover, can know your boundlessness? You are (one with) the Fearless, Formless Lord; you speak the Unspeakable, and to you alone has its understanding been given. O world, strayed in doubt, when (the Lord) is meditated on by the Guru's teaching, you are freed from births and from death, and no punishment of Jam falls (on you). O foolish mind, O mortal, reflect, and repeat (the Name) day and night: through the Perfect True Guru, righteous living and good deeds are attained. ॥2॥
1398.7: Again and again I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's True Name. What comparison can I offer, what service can I perform? With both palms joined, facing him, savour (his Name) with your tongue. And know him in thought, word and deed; believe in no other anywhere; the Guru has given that infinite, sublime Name as the heart's support. O poet Nal, (it is the Name) remembering which (is as when) glass turns to gold at the touch of the paaras, and other trees take on the fragrance of sandalwood. Seeing whose door, lust and anger are driven away: again and again I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's True Name. ॥3॥
Nal too is one of the Bhatts.
1399.1: He gave Guru Ram Das the throne of Raj and Jog. First (Guru) Nanak (rose) like the moon, and the world was filled with joy; to carry people across, he spread his light. To Guru Angad he gave the treasure, the knowledge of the Unspoken; (Guru Angad) brought the five fiends (the passions) under control, and no fear arises (in him). Guru Amar (Das), the revered True Guru, kept (people's) honour in the Kalyug; on seeing his lotus feet, sins depart. When (Guru Amar Das's) mind was satisfied in every way, then he was pleased, and gave Guru Ram Das the throne of Raj and Jog. ॥4॥
1399.2: Radd (a metre). That which holds up the earth and the sky, and made the air, the waters of the lakes, fire, food and the rest; which gave the moon and the stars to the night and the sun to the day, the mountains, and fruit and flowers to the trees; which made gods, men and the seven seas, and upholds the three worlds: that one Name, the Lord's Name, is true for ever; (Guru Ram Das) has received (it), the light, from Guru Amar (Das). ॥1॥
1399.3: Whoever heard the Guru's Shabad with his ears turned from glass into gold. Whoever uttered the True Guru's Name with his mouth turned from poison into Amrit. Iron becomes a ruby when the True Guru casts his gracious glance. Those who reflect on the knowledge the Guru has spoken, he turns from stones into jewels. The True Guru has turned (them) from wood into sandalwood, and their pain and poverty are gone, those who touched the True Guru's feet: from beasts and ghosts they became gods and men. ॥2॥
1399.4: When the Guru is on one's side, what pride is there in wealth? When the Guru is on one's side, what can a hundred thousand arms (armies) do? When the Guru is on one's side, knowledge and meditation are set on none other (than the Lord). When the Guru is on one's side, the Shabad becomes manifest (within), and he (abides) in the home of the True One. The servant, the Bhatt, offers this prayer: whoever repeats Guru, Guru day and night, whoever enshrines the Guru's Name in his heart, is spared both birth and death. ॥3॥
1399.5: Without the Guru all is pitch dark; without the Guru, no understanding comes. Without the Guru, awareness (of God) does not awaken, nor does success come; without the Guru, liberation is not attained. Take the Guru: this is the true counsel; take the Guru, O my mind. Take the Guru, rich in the Shabad, and all your sins will be cut away. The poet Nal says: keep the Guru in your eyes, the Guru in your words, the Guru, the Guru; the Guru is true for ever. Those who have not seen the Guru, nor taken (him as their Guru), are fruitless in the world. ॥4॥
1399.6: O my mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru. In the Kalyug (the Guru) is the boat able to carry (all) across; hearing his words, one enters samadhi. And he is the hero who destroys sorrows and gives peace; whoever meditates on him, he dwells near that one. He is the perfect being, remembering the Lord in his heart; seeing his face, sins are driven away. If you want divine understanding, riddhis and siddhis, O my mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru. ॥5॥
1400.1: Beholding the Guru's face, I have found great peace. The thirst I had to drink Amrit: to fulfil that longing, the Creator has brought about the meeting. My mind, which ran in the ten directions after pleasures and desires, is fulfilled and has settled in its place. (The Guru) has built Gobindwal, like the city of Gobind, on the bank of the waters of the Beas. The pain of years has gone far away; beholding the Guru's face, I have found great peace. ॥6॥
Gobindwal is the town Guru Amar Das Ji built on the bank of the river Beas (today Goindwal).
1400.2: The all-powerful Guru has laid his hand on (his) head. The Guru showed grace and gave (him) the Lord's Name, the Guru whose feet, once seen, take away sins. Night and day (his) meditation (on the Name) stays unbroken, the Name hearing which the son of the Sun (Jam) is afraid. The servant says: (Guru Ram Das) puts his hope in the Guru of the world alone; meeting the paaras, he has himself been made a paaras. The Lord has made Guru Ram Das everlasting: the all-powerful Guru has laid his hand on (his) head. ॥7॥
The son of the Sun: in the Puranas, Jam (Dharam Raj) is the son of the Sun.
1400.3: Now save the honour of your servant, the Bhatt, as you saved the honour of the devotee Prahlad, tearing Harnakhash apart with the nails of your hands. And, O Lord God, you saved Dropati's honour: as her clothes were being stripped, you gave (her) garments in plenty. You saved Sodama from misfortune; as Ganika recited (the Name), you fulfilled all her affairs. O revered True Guru, be gracious in this Kalyug, and save the honour of your servant, the Bhatt. ॥8॥

Dropati (Draupadi): in the Mahabharata, the wife of the Pandavas, dragged by the Kauravas before the full court to be stripped; she called on Krishna, and her cloth never came to an end. Sodama (Sudama): Krishna's poor Brahmin friend, made rich by him. Ganika: a courtesan, saved by teaching a parrot to say Ram.
1400.4: Jholna (a metre). O mortals, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru. Know this as true: (the Guru) repeats the Shabad of the Lord, Har Har, bestows the Name, the nine treasures, and with his tongue relishes (it) day and night. And the colour of (the Lord's) love is obtained when one meditates through the Guru; O wise ones, give up other paths and worship the Lord. Keep the Guru's words in your heart, bring (the self made of) the five elements under control, redeem your life and your lineage, and you will be honoured at the Lord's door. If you long for every comfort here and hereafter, O mortals, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru. ॥1॥
1400.5: Repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, holding it true. Keeping the Guru's words in your heart, enshrine in your mind the Lord, the all-knowing, the unfathomable treasure of virtues, and meditate on him day and night. And bathe in the Guru, the pure, fathomless water; O Sants, O Sikhs of the Guru, swim in the pool of the love of the True Name. (The Guru) ever repeats (the Name of) the Formless One, free of enmity and of fear, and in the relish of love for the Guru's Shabad he makes devotion to the Lord firm. O foolish mind, give up doubt; worship the Name through the Guru; repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, holding it true. ॥2॥
1401.1: Repeat Guru, Guru, Guru; through the Guru, the Lord is found. The Guru is an ocean, deep, profound and boundless, (holding) the gems, diamonds and jewels of the Lord's Name; meeting him, the attention is fixed (on the Lord). And the Guru is a sweet fragrance; his touch turns (one) to gold; he takes away the filth of evil-mindedness; let the Guru be meditated on through the Shabad. At whose door streams of Amrit ever flow, in that pure pool of the Guru's knowledge the Sants and Sikhs bathe. Enshrine in your heart the Lord's Name, the treasure that frees from all desire; repeat Guru, Guru, Guru; through the Guru, the Lord is found. ॥3॥
1401.2: O mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru. Serving him, and hearing the Guru's words with their ears, Shiva, the Siddhas, the seekers, gods, demons, (Shiva's) ganas and the thirty-three (crore gods) cross over. And those Sants and devotees cross over who lovingly repeat Guru, Guru; meeting the Guru, Prahlad crossed over, and the silent sages (too). Narad and the others, Sanak and his brothers, cross over through the Guru, (one with) the Lord; attached to the one Name they cross over; (O mind,) give up other tastes. The servant offers this prayer: the Name is found through the Guru; O mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru. ॥4॥
1401.3: The revered Guru, the Master, is above all, he who in the Satjug showed grace to Dhru, saved the devotee, the revered Prahlad, and placed his lotus hand on his forehead. His form is beyond knowing; beings cannot comprehend it. The seekers and the Siddhas, all are in his refuge. Hold the Guru's words in your heart as true, and carry your human birth and body across. The Guru is the ship and the Guru the oarsman; no one has ever crossed over without the Guru. By the Guru's grace God is found; without the Guru, there is no liberation. Guru Nanak dwells close to Banwari (the Master of the world). He installed Lahna (as Guru) and set (his) light in the world. Lahna made the path of righteousness run, and gave (it) to Amar Das the Bhalla. He established the revered Ram Das, the Sodhi, firm for ever, and bestowed (on him) the Lord's Name, the treasure that never runs out. He bestowed the Lord's Name, the treasure that never runs out, (lasting) through the four ages; by serving the Guru this fruit is obtained. Those who bow at his feet find peace in his refuge; they enjoy supreme bliss, and are called Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru). The Supreme Lord, the Master, the primal one, who sustains and nourishes (all), is visible in (the Guru's) body. Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across. He whose Amrit words, his bani, the holy repeat in their hearts with eager love:
Sodhi is a clan: Guru Ram Das Ji was a Sodhi.
1401.4: the sight of that Guru is joy and gladness for ever, and bears fruit in the world. In the world the Guru's sight is fruitful as the Ganga; touching (his feet), one reaches the supremely pure state. Even mortals who have fallen conquer the realm of Jam, becoming the Lord's servants, dyed in the knowledge of the Guru, the giver of bliss. He is the beautiful jewel of Raghu's clan, (born) in Dasrath's house, whose refuge the sages long for. Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across. ॥2॥
Shri Ram was born in Raghu's clan, in the house of Dasrath; the Bhatt praises the Guru in that form.
1402.1: The world is a fathomless ocean; the Lord's Name is the raft, obtained through the Guru. When this faith has come into the heart, birth and death in the world are ended. Those in whose hearts faith has come have reached the high state. They have given up attachment to Maya, greed and craving, and the pain of lust and anger has left them. They have beheld God, the cause of creation, whose sight is divine, and all their doubt is gone. Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across. ॥3॥
1402.2: The Guru's glory is ever manifest in every heart, and his praise in (the hearts of) his servants. Some read, hear and sing (his praise), and bathe at the break of dawn. Bathing at dawn, they worship the Guru with a pure mind and in due form. Touching the paaras, their body becomes gold, and they meditate on (the Guru), the embodiment of light. The life of the world, the master of the world, pervades the waters and the land in many forms and colours. Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across. ॥4॥
1402.3: Those who have taken (the Guru's) word as unshakable, as Dhru did, are the beings saved from death. They have crossed the terrible ocean in an instant; (to them) the world is made like the shadow of a cloud. In the Sat Sangat the coiled knot (of their minds) has come undone, and through the Guru they glow with supreme bliss. The revered Guru, the Master, is above all; let the True One be served in thought, word and deed. ॥5॥
Kundalini: in yoga, a power held to lie coiled asleep in the body; here the coil of the mind tangled in Maya, which comes undone in the Sat Sangat.
1402.4: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved. Lotus-eyed, sweet of speech, beautiful amid millions of companions, (you are the one) whom mother Jasod would urge: eat curd and rice, dear one. Seeing your peerless beauty she was lost in love, when you played and the bells of your waistband jingled. The pen of death and the command are in your hand: tell me, who can erase (them)? Shiva and Brahma long to hold your knowledge and meditation in their hearts. You alone are ever the True, the Eternal, the abode of Lakshmi, the Primal Being: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved. ॥1॥
Vahi, vah: wondrous (a cry of awe and praise); Waheguru is the Wondrous Guru, the Name by which Sikhs remember God.
In these swayye the Bhatt praises the Guru in the form of Krishna: Jasod (Yashoda) was Krishna's foster-mother. Sri Nivas: the abode of Lakshmi, a name of Vishnu.
1402.5: Your name is Ram, your abode the highest; pure is your understanding; formless, beyond count: who can equal you? Steady of mind, for your devotee's sake you took on a form (as Narasimha), and slew Harnakhash, tearing him open with your nails. (Yours are) the conch, the discus, the mace and the lotus; you yourself took on a guise of guile; you are the infinite Paarbrahm (the Supreme Lord): who can know you? You alone are ever the True, the Eternal, the abode of Lakshmi, the Primal Being: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved. ॥2॥
The conch, discus, mace and lotus are Vishnu's emblems. The guise of guile: the Vaman incarnation.
1402.6: Clad in yellow, your teeth white as the kund flower, your beloved beside you, a garland at your throat, you gladly wear on your head a crown of peacock feathers. You need no minister; you are greatly patient, righteousness embodied, beyond knowing and beyond reach; you have staged this play for your own delight. Your story is beyond telling and cannot be told; you pervade the three worlds; of your own will you have taken this form, O King of kings. You alone are ever the True, the Eternal, the abode of Lakshmi, the Primal Being: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved. ॥3॥
Kund: a white jasmine. The beloved: Radha. The yellow garments and the crown of peacock feathers are Krishna's marks.
1403.1: Gubind (the Lord of the universe) himself is the True Guru, the True Guru, the True Guru. He is the deceiver of Bali, the crusher of the mighty, who makes devotion bear fruit, the prince Kanh (Krishna); he is Nihkalank (the stainless one to come), whose drum sounds, with whom the hosts of the sun and moon will march. He is Ram, who pervades all, the destroyer of sins, who brings well-being to all the worlds; he himself is in all beings; he is the god of gods, and the thousand-mouthed king of serpents. He took birth and did his deeds as the fish, the tortoise and the boar, and played the game of ball on the bank of the Jamuna. O mind of Gayand, enshrine the sublime Name in your heart and give up vice: Gubind himself is the True Guru, the True Guru, the True Guru. ॥4॥

Nihkalank: Kalki, the incarnation to come in the Puranas. The king of serpents: Shesh Nag. The fish, the tortoise and the boar are Vishnu's incarnations; the game of ball by the Jamuna is Krishna's. Gayand too is one of the Bhatts.
1403.2: The revered Guru, the revered Guru, the revered Guru is true for ever. Accept what the Guru says as your own treasure, and know this mantra as true: night and day it brings well-being, and you will attain the supreme state. Give up lust, anger, greed and attachment, and deceit towards everyone; cut the noose of Haumai (ego), and love the Saadh Sangat. Body, home, love of a wife: this world is the play of the mind; ever serve (the Guru's) lotus feet, and make your understanding firm. O mind of Gayand, enshrine the sublime Name in your heart and give up vice: the revered Guru, the revered Guru, the revered Guru is true for ever. ॥5॥
1403.3: Age after age you fill (the hearts of) your servants; O Waheguru, all is your blessing. You are the Formless Lord, ever intact; no one can say since when you have been. You created countless Brahmas and Vishnus; they fell into attachment to the pride of their own minds. You brought forth the eighty-four lakh species, and since then have given sustenance to them all. Age after age you fill (the hearts of) your servants; O Waheguru, all is your blessing. ॥1॥
Vahguru and Vahiguru are two spellings of the one word Waheguru. The eighty-four lakh (8.4 million) species: by tradition, all the kinds of being through which a soul passes from birth to birth.
1403.4: Vast is the play of the Wondrous One. He himself laughs, he himself thinks; he himself gives light to the sun and the moon. He is the water, he the land and what holds it up; he himself has made his dwelling in every heart. He himself is man, and he himself woman; he himself is the piece, and he himself the dice. O Sangat, all of you, reflect through the Guru: vast is the play of the Wondrous One. ॥2॥
The piece and the dice: of the game of chaupar.
1403.5: You have made this play, this great meeting (of the elements), this spectacle; O Waheguru, all creation is yours. You pervade the water, the land, the sky and the netherworld; your words are sweeter than Amrit. Brahma and the rest, Rudra (Shiva) and the rest, revere you; you are the death of death; O Immaculate One, (all) beg of you. By the Guru's grace the highest good is obtained, and the mind is bound to the Sat Sangat. You have made this play, this great meeting (of the elements), this spectacle; O Waheguru, all creation is yours. ॥3॥
1404.1: He who is beyond reach, endless and without beginning, whose beginning no one knows, on whom Shiva and Biranchi (Brahma) meditate daily, whom the Veda describes, formless and without enmity, with no second other than him, able to break and to fashion, that God is the boat that carries across; he who made the world in many forms, his servant Mathura savours with his tongue. The revered True Name, the Creator, the all-pervading Being, dwells in the mind of Guru Ram Das. ॥1॥
Mathura too is one of the Bhatts.
1404.2: I have taken hold of the all-powerful Guru, to gain steady understanding and good counsel, whose banner of righteousness ever flies; (I hold to him) to drive away the heaps and waves of sin. Knowing it, his servant Mathura has spoken this truth from the heart, and there is nothing else to consider: in the Kalyug, the great ship that ferries (us) over the world-ocean is the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
1404.3: Constantly, in the company of the Sat Sangat, dyed in a beautiful colour, they sing (the Lord's) praise. The Sustainer of the earth has himself laid down the path of righteousness; they stay absorbed in him and do not wander. Mathura says: good is their fortune, and they obtain the fruits their minds desire. What fear of the son of the Sun can they have who fix their minds on the Guru's feet? ॥3॥
1404.4: (The Guru is a pool) brimming with the pure nectar of the Name; before daybreak the waves of the Shabad rise in it. It is deep, profound, unfathomable and vast, ever brimming over, in every way a mine of jewels. The Sants, like swans, delight in it; their fear of Jam and the record of their sorrows are wiped out. To drive away the sins of the Kalyug, the sight of the Guru is an ocean of every peace. ॥4॥
1404.5: He on whom the sages meditate, wandering through all the ages, while only now and then does one find the inner light; whose praise Biranchi sings with the words of the Vedas; holding to whom, Shiva the sage does not leave Kailash; for whom countless yogis, celibates, Siddhas and seekers practise austerities, and wander about detached, in the guise of matted locks: that True Guru, of his own gracious will, showed mercy to all beings, and gave Guru Ram Das the glory of the Name. ॥5॥
Kailash: the Himalayan mountain held to be Shiva's abode.
1404.6: (He has) the treasure of the Name; his meditation is turned within; the mass of his radiance shines through the three worlds. Beholding his sight, doubt flees in confusion, sorrows are cast off, and the joys of Sahaj blossom. His servants and Sikhs are ever drawn to him, as swarms of bees to the fragrance of a flower. The Guru, while still present (in body), himself established the true throne of Guru Ram Das, firm for ever. ॥6॥
1405.1: He has carried across the world, entranced by the intoxication of Maya, giving it the all-powerful Amrit Name. And he is glorious, ever rich in peace and wealth; riddhis and siddhis never leave his side. He is a great giver, of boundless might: his servant and slave (Mathura) has told this truth. Why should he care for anyone, on whose head the Guru has laid his hand? ॥7॥
1405.2: He alone pervades the three worlds; he has made no one in the world like himself; he himself brought himself forth; gods, men and demons have not found his end. The gods, the demons, men, the ganas and the Gandharbs have not found his end, though they went searching. He is imperishable, unmoving, beyond birth, self-existent, the highest Being, infinite and beyond all. He alone is ever the cause of creation, all-powerful; all beings have meditated on him in their minds. O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥1॥
1405.3: The True Guru Nanak worshipped with a single mind, and gave his body, mind and wealth to Gobind. (Guru) Angad enshrined within himself the One of endless forms; with the knowledge of the Unreachable, his heart was steeped in love. Guru Amar Das won the Creator over; he meditated on him, crying Wah, Wah. O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥2॥
1405.4: Narad, Dhru, Prahlad and Sudama, who are counted the Lord's devotees of former ages; Ambrik, Jaidev, Trilochan, Nama and Kabir too, who are named: (of them, those) born in the Kalyug, their praise has spread over the whole world. O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥3॥
1405.5: (O Guru,) those who remember you with the mind, their lust and anger are erased. Those who remember you with speech, their pain and poverty are erased in an instant. Those who touch your sight through their deeds become like the paaras; Bal the Bhatt has sung (your) praise. O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥4॥
Bal too is one of the Bhatts.
1405.6: The True Guru, remembering whom the darkness of the eyes is gone in an instant; remembering whom the Lord's Name (grows) in the heart day by day; remembering whom one stills the burning within the soul; remembering whom one obtains riddhis, siddhis and the nine treasures: Bal says: that is Guru Ram Das; join the Sangat and call (him) blessed, blessed. The True Guru, clinging to whom God is found: remember that True Guru, O people. ॥5॥
1405.7: He who lived the Shabad and attained the supreme state, and in his service never left (the Guru's) side: from him the pearl of knowledge has shone forth, and its light destroys sorrow, poverty and darkness. O poet Kirat, those who turn (from the world) and fall at the feet of that Sant have no fear of lust, anger or Jam. As Angad was ever at Guru Nanak's side, so is Guru Ram Das with Guru Amar Das. ॥1॥
1406.1: He who served the True Guru and obtained the treasure (of the Name), who dwells night and day at the Lord's feet: and so the whole vast Sangat honours you with love and reverence; you are the sandalwood of Malyagar, your fragrance spreading for all to know. The light that welled up in Dhru, Prahlad, Kabir and Tilochan as they took the Name, seeing which great joy fills the mind, is Guru Ram Das, the support of the Sants. ॥2॥
Malyagar: the sandalwood of the Malaya mountains, whose fragrance makes even the trees around it fragrant.
1406.2: (Guru) Nanak recognised the Name of the Immaculate One, and worshipped (him), fixing his attention in love. From him came Angad, an ocean (of virtues), ever at his side; he laid the foundation of joining the attention to the Shabad. The story of Guru Amar Das cannot be told: with one tongue nothing of it can be said. Now, to carry the whole world across, the glory has come to Guru Ram Das, the Sodhi. ॥3॥
1406.3: We are full of faults, without a single virtue; leaving the Amrit, we have eaten poison, nothing but poison. Fallen into attachment to Maya and into doubt, we have gone astray, and have given our love to sons and wife. We have heard of one sublime path, the Guru's Sangat; joining it, the fear of Jam has been wiped out. Kirat the Bhatt has one prayer: O Guru Ram Das, keep (me) in your refuge. ॥4॥
1406.4: (O Guru Ram Das,) you have crushed attachment and brought it under your sway; seizing lust by the hair, you have thrown it to the ground. With your might you have cut anger to pieces, and driven greed away in disgrace. Birth and death, with palms joined, obey whatever your command may be. You have bound the world-ocean, and, well pleased, carried the Sikhs across. Over your head is the royal canopy, and your throne is true; you are mighty, joining Jog and worldly enjoyment. Sal speaks the truth: O Guru Ram Das, your rule is unshakable, and your army unbroken. ॥1॥
1406.5: In all four ages you are the True Guru; you yourself are the Supreme God. From the very first, gods, men, seekers, Siddhas and Sikhs have been your servants. You are from the beginning, from the start of the ages, without beginning; your power upholds the three worlds. You are the saviour of the Agam and the Nigam; you ride upon old age and Jam. Guru Amar Das has established you, firm for ever; you have gone across, and are the boat that carries (others) across. The poet Sal heeds neither sin nor Death: O Guru Ram Das, (he is in) your refuge. ॥2॥
Agam and Nigam: the Shastras and the Vedas, the Hindu scriptures.

1396.3: Swayye in praise of the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
With a one-pointed mind may I meditate on the all-pervading Lord, untouched by Maya;
by the Guru's grace may I ever sing the Lord's virtues;
and, as I sing them, may my mind blossom.
O True Guru, fulfil this hope of your servant.
He who, by serving the True Guru, has attained the supreme state,
and has meditated on the Imperishable, Unmanifest Lord:
meeting him, poverty does not cling (to anyone);
I utter the spotless virtues of that noble servant (of God) within whom the Name, the Amrit, has welled up.
Serving the True Guru, he has found the relish of the Shabad and enshrined the Name of the Immaculate One in his heart.
He delights in the Lord's Name, seeks out Gobind's virtues, longs for the Essence (the Lord), and is a pool of even-mindedness.
O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥1॥
1396.4: (He is) a pool of Amrit, ever full, from which flow streams of Amrit that give the immortal state.
Those Sants drink of it and bathe (in it) within their minds who have done service before (in past lives).
Driving out their fear, he has given them the state of fearlessness, and by the Shabad alone he has carried them across.
O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥2॥
1396.5: The True Guru's understanding is deep, his Sat Sangat is pure, and his soul is dyed deep red in (the Lord's) love.
His mind is awake, the lotus (of his heart) has opened in Sahaj, and he has found the fearless, immaculate Lord in his own home (within).
The compassionate True Guru has made the Lord's Name firm (in him); by its grace he has brought the five (passions: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under control.
O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥3॥
1397.1: Through reflection he has come to know (the Lord) directly, and his attention is fixed on the One who has no parts; he has met the paaras (the touchstone that turns iron to gold: the Guru), and (dwells) in the home of Sahaj.
By the True Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state, and with loving devotion his storehouses are full.
He has erased birth and death, the fear of dying has fled, and his mind is fixed on the pool of contentment.
O poet Kal, Guru Ram Das, son of Thakur Hardas, fills the empty pools (of hearts). ॥4॥
1397.2: He has found the Infinite, who fills the empty, and enshrined him within his heart;
in his mind he has reflected on the Essence, the destroyer of sorrow, who awakens the soul.
Ever in joy, in the Lord's love, he alone knows the taste of that love.
By the True Guru's grace he enjoys (the Lord's) love in Sahaj.
By (Guru) Nanak's grace and (Guru) Angad's wise understanding, Guru Amar Das made (the Lord's) command prevail.
Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have attained the unshakable, immortal state. ॥5॥
1397.3: He dwells in the pool of contentment, and with his tongue he brings forth the taste of Amrit.
Meeting him, peace wells up, and sin flees far away.
He has obtained the ocean of peace, given (by the Guru), and on the Lord's path he does not tire.
His armour of self-restraint, truth, contentment and gentle nature never breaks.
The Creator has made him the True Guru, approved (by him), and the world has sounded the trumpet of his praise.
Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have attained the fearless, immortal state. ॥6॥
1397.4: With the True Guru's approval he has won the world, and in his mind he has meditated on the One.
Blessed, blessed is the True Guru Amar Das, who made the Name firm (in him).
The treasure of the Name is (for him) the nine treasures; riddhis and siddhis are his handmaids.
He has found the pool of Sahaj; he has met the imperishable, all-pervading Lord.
The Name, holding to which the devotees from the very beginning have crossed over, the Guru has made firm in him.
Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have obtained the priceless gift of the Lord's love. ॥7॥
1397.5: Streams of loving devotion (flow in him); his love from of old never runs dry.
Through the True Guru's fathomless Shabad he drinks deep the taste of the streams of Amrit.
Wisdom is his mother, contentment his father; he is absorbed in the pool of Sahaj.
He is beyond birth, self-existent; by the Guru's word he has carried the world across.
(One with the Lord,) unmanifest, beyond the reach of the senses and infinite, he has enshrined the Guru's Shabad in his mind.
Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have found the saviour of the world. ॥8॥
1397.6: That saviour of the world, store of the nine treasures, carries his devotees across the world-ocean;
the Lord's Name, a drop of Amrit, takes away the poison of the world.
The tree of Sahaj has borne fruit: the Amrit fruits of divine knowledge hang on it.
They are obtained by the Guru's grace; blessed are those fortunate people (who receive them).
They have been liberated through the True Guru's Shabad, (they who) have found love for the Guru in their minds.
Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, you have sounded the drum of the Shabad. ॥9॥
1398.1: Faith is his couch, Sahaj his canopy, contentment the wall of his tent, and an ever-gentle nature the armour that adorns him.
Through the Guru's Shabad he has lived (the Name); the Name is his support, and he makes those around him fragrant (with it).
Beyond birth, good and stainless, he dwells with the True Guru.
Kal says: O Guru Ram Das, your dwelling is in the pool of Sahaj. ॥10॥
1398.2: Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, in their hearts he makes the Lord's Name dwell.
Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, sin flees far from them.
Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, he takes away their pride and conceit.
Those with whom the Guru is well pleased, he attaches them to the Shabad and carries them across the world-ocean.
Those who have found a true bond with the Guru, their birth in the world has borne fruit.
O poet Kal, hasten to the refuge of the revered Guru; worldly gifts and liberation all (come) by clinging to the Guru. ॥11॥
1398.3: The True Guru has pitched a tent, and under it throngs from all the ages have gathered.
Direct knowledge (of God) is its pole and the Name its prop, by which the devotees are fulfilled.
Guru Nanak, Angad and Amar (Das), devotees, have merged in the Lord.
O Guru Ram Das, you too have known the relish of this Raj and Jog. ॥12॥
1398.4: He alone is a Janak who has known (the Lord) and set the chariot (of his mind) in the state of unman;
who has practised truth and contentment, and filled the empty pool (of the mind).
The story of the immortal city (the unshakable state) cannot be told; he alone obtains it to whom (the Lord) gives it.
O Guru Ram Das, this kingdom of Janak befits you alone. ॥13॥
1398.5: Whoever repeats the True Guru's Name in his mind, firmly, with attention fixed on the One: tell me, how can sorrow and sin come to such people?
(The Guru) is the boat that carries across: the one on whom he casts his glance even for an instant reflects on the Shabad in his heart, and loses his lust and anger.
He is the giver to all beings, who makes known the knowledge of the Unreachable; day and night he holds to meditation, and does not sleep even for a moment.
Seeing him, poverty departs; one obtains that treasure, the Name, and through the Guru, by (his) knowledge, washes away the filth of evil-mindedness.
Whoever repeats the True Guru's Name in his mind, firmly, with attention fixed on the One: tell me, how can sorrow and sin come to such people? ॥1॥
1398.6: Through the Perfect True Guru, righteous living and good deeds are attained.
He whose service the Siddhas, the Saadhs, the silent sages, gods and men beg for has fixed his single-pointed attention on the sublime Shabad.
Who, moreover, can know your boundlessness? You are (one with) the Fearless, Formless Lord; you speak the Unspeakable, and to you alone has its understanding been given.
O world, strayed in doubt, when (the Lord) is meditated on by the Guru's teaching, you are freed from births and from death, and no punishment of Jam falls (on you).
O foolish mind, O mortal, reflect, and repeat (the Name) day and night: through the Perfect True Guru, righteous living and good deeds are attained. ॥2॥
1398.7: Again and again I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's True Name.
What comparison can I offer, what service can I perform? With both palms joined, facing him, savour (his Name) with your tongue.
And know him in thought, word and deed; believe in no other anywhere; the Guru has given that infinite, sublime Name as the heart's support.
O poet Nal, (it is the Name) remembering which (is as when) glass turns to gold at the touch of the paaras, and other trees take on the fragrance of sandalwood.
Seeing whose door, lust and anger are driven away: again and again I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's True Name. ॥3॥
1399.1: He gave Guru Ram Das the throne of Raj and Jog.
First (Guru) Nanak (rose) like the moon, and the world was filled with joy; to carry people across, he spread his light.
To Guru Angad he gave the treasure, the knowledge of the Unspoken; (Guru Angad) brought the five fiends (the passions) under control, and no fear arises (in him).
Guru Amar (Das), the revered True Guru, kept (people's) honour in the Kalyug; on seeing his lotus feet, sins depart.
When (Guru Amar Das's) mind was satisfied in every way, then he was pleased, and gave Guru Ram Das the throne of Raj and Jog. ॥4॥
1399.2: That which holds up the earth and the sky, and made the air, the waters of the lakes, fire, food and the rest;
which gave the moon and the stars to the night and the sun to the day, the mountains, and fruit and flowers to the trees;
which made gods, men and the seven seas, and upholds the three worlds:
that one Name, the Lord's Name, is true for ever; (Guru Ram Das) has received (it), the light, from Guru Amar (Das). ॥1॥
1399.3: Whoever heard the Guru's Shabad with his ears turned from glass into gold.
Whoever uttered the True Guru's Name with his mouth turned from poison into Amrit.
Iron becomes a ruby when the True Guru casts his gracious glance.
Those who reflect on the knowledge the Guru has spoken, he turns from stones into jewels.
The True Guru has turned (them) from wood into sandalwood, and their pain and poverty are gone,
those who touched the True Guru's feet: from beasts and ghosts they became gods and men. ॥2॥
1399.4: When the Guru is on one's side, what pride is there in wealth?
When the Guru is on one's side, what can a hundred thousand arms (armies) do?
When the Guru is on one's side, knowledge and meditation are set on none other (than the Lord).
When the Guru is on one's side, the Shabad becomes manifest (within), and he (abides) in the home of the True One.
The servant, the Bhatt, offers this prayer: whoever repeats Guru, Guru day and night,
whoever enshrines the Guru's Name in his heart, is spared both birth and death. ॥3॥
1399.5: Without the Guru all is pitch dark; without the Guru, no understanding comes.
Without the Guru, awareness (of God) does not awaken, nor does success come; without the Guru, liberation is not attained.
Take the Guru: this is the true counsel; take the Guru, O my mind.
Take the Guru, rich in the Shabad, and all your sins will be cut away.
The poet Nal says: keep the Guru in your eyes, the Guru in your words, the Guru, the Guru; the Guru is true for ever.
Those who have not seen the Guru, nor taken (him as their Guru), are fruitless in the world. ॥4॥
1399.6: O my mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru.
In the Kalyug (the Guru) is the boat able to carry (all) across; hearing his words, one enters samadhi.
And he is the hero who destroys sorrows and gives peace; whoever meditates on him, he dwells near that one.
He is the perfect being, remembering the Lord in his heart; seeing his face, sins are driven away.
If you want divine understanding, riddhis and siddhis, O my mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru. ॥5॥
1400.1: Beholding the Guru's face, I have found great peace.
The thirst I had to drink Amrit: to fulfil that longing, the Creator has brought about the meeting.
My mind, which ran in the ten directions after pleasures and desires, is fulfilled and has settled in its place.
(The Guru) has built Gobindwal, like the city of Gobind, on the bank of the waters of the Beas.
The pain of years has gone far away; beholding the Guru's face, I have found great peace. ॥6॥
1400.2: The all-powerful Guru has laid his hand on (his) head.
The Guru showed grace and gave (him) the Lord's Name, the Guru whose feet, once seen, take away sins.
Night and day (his) meditation (on the Name) stays unbroken, the Name hearing which the son of the Sun (Jam) is afraid.
The servant says: (Guru Ram Das) puts his hope in the Guru of the world alone; meeting the paaras, he has himself been made a paaras.
The Lord has made Guru Ram Das everlasting: the all-powerful Guru has laid his hand on (his) head. ॥7॥
1400.3: Now save the honour of your servant, the Bhatt,
as you saved the honour of the devotee Prahlad, tearing Harnakhash apart with the nails of your hands.
And, O Lord God, you saved Dropati's honour: as her clothes were being stripped, you gave (her) garments in plenty.
You saved Sodama from misfortune; as Ganika recited (the Name), you fulfilled all her affairs.
O revered True Guru, be gracious in this Kalyug, and save the honour of your servant, the Bhatt. ॥8॥
1400.4: O mortals, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru.
Know this as true: (the Guru) repeats the Shabad of the Lord, Har Har, bestows the Name, the nine treasures, and with his tongue relishes (it) day and night.
And the colour of (the Lord's) love is obtained when one meditates through the Guru; O wise ones, give up other paths and worship the Lord.
Keep the Guru's words in your heart, bring (the self made of) the five elements under control, redeem your life and your lineage, and you will be honoured at the Lord's door.
If you long for every comfort here and hereafter, O mortals, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru. ॥1॥
1400.5: Repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, holding it true.
Keeping the Guru's words in your heart, enshrine in your mind the Lord, the all-knowing, the unfathomable treasure of virtues, and meditate on him day and night.
And bathe in the Guru, the pure, fathomless water; O Sants, O Sikhs of the Guru, swim in the pool of the love of the True Name.
(The Guru) ever repeats (the Name of) the Formless One, free of enmity and of fear, and in the relish of love for the Guru's Shabad he makes devotion to the Lord firm.
O foolish mind, give up doubt; worship the Name through the Guru; repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, holding it true. ॥2॥
1401.1: Repeat Guru, Guru, Guru; through the Guru, the Lord is found.
The Guru is an ocean, deep, profound and boundless, (holding) the gems, diamonds and jewels of the Lord's Name; meeting him, the attention is fixed (on the Lord).
And the Guru is a sweet fragrance; his touch turns (one) to gold; he takes away the filth of evil-mindedness; let the Guru be meditated on through the Shabad.
At whose door streams of Amrit ever flow, in that pure pool of the Guru's knowledge the Sants and Sikhs bathe.
Enshrine in your heart the Lord's Name, the treasure that frees from all desire; repeat Guru, Guru, Guru; through the Guru, the Lord is found. ॥3॥
1401.2: O mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru.
Serving him, and hearing the Guru's words with their ears, Shiva, the Siddhas, the seekers, gods, demons, (Shiva's) ganas and the thirty-three (crore gods) cross over.
And those Sants and devotees cross over who lovingly repeat Guru, Guru; meeting the Guru, Prahlad crossed over, and the silent sages (too).
Narad and the others, Sanak and his brothers, cross over through the Guru, (one with) the Lord; attached to the one Name they cross over; (O mind,) give up other tastes.
The servant offers this prayer: the Name is found through the Guru; O mind, repeat Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru. ॥4॥
1401.3: The revered Guru, the Master, is above all,
he who in the Satjug showed grace to Dhru,
saved the devotee, the revered Prahlad,
and placed his lotus hand on his forehead.
His form is beyond knowing; beings cannot comprehend it.
The seekers and the Siddhas, all are in his refuge.
Hold the Guru's words in your heart as true,
and carry your human birth and body across.
The Guru is the ship and the Guru the oarsman; no one has ever crossed over without the Guru.
By the Guru's grace God is found; without the Guru, there is no liberation.
Guru Nanak dwells close to Banwari (the Master of the world).
He installed Lahna (as Guru) and set (his) light in the world.
Lahna made the path of righteousness run,
and gave (it) to Amar Das the Bhalla.
He established the revered Ram Das, the Sodhi, firm for ever,
and bestowed (on him) the Lord's Name, the treasure that never runs out.
He bestowed the Lord's Name, the treasure that never runs out, (lasting) through the four ages; by serving the Guru this fruit is obtained.
Those who bow at his feet find peace in his refuge; they enjoy supreme bliss, and are called Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru).
The Supreme Lord, the Master, the primal one, who sustains and nourishes (all), is visible in (the Guru's) body.
Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across.
He whose Amrit words, his bani, the holy repeat in their hearts with eager love:
1401.4: the sight of that Guru is joy and gladness for ever, and bears fruit in the world.
In the world the Guru's sight is fruitful as the Ganga; touching (his feet), one reaches the supremely pure state.
Even mortals who have fallen conquer the realm of Jam, becoming the Lord's servants, dyed in the knowledge of the Guru, the giver of bliss.
He is the beautiful jewel of Raghu's clan, (born) in Dasrath's house, whose refuge the sages long for.
Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across. ॥2॥
1402.1: The world is a fathomless ocean; the Lord's Name is the raft, obtained through the Guru.
When this faith has come into the heart, birth and death in the world are ended.
Those in whose hearts faith has come have reached the high state.
They have given up attachment to Maya, greed and craving, and the pain of lust and anger has left them.
They have beheld God, the cause of creation, whose sight is divine, and all their doubt is gone.
Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across. ॥3॥
1402.2: The Guru's glory is ever manifest in every heart, and his praise in (the hearts of) his servants.
Some read, hear and sing (his praise), and bathe at the break of dawn.
Bathing at dawn, they worship the Guru with a pure mind and in due form.
Touching the paaras, their body becomes gold, and they meditate on (the Guru), the embodiment of light.
The life of the world, the master of the world, pervades the waters and the land in many forms and colours.
Serve the Guru, the True Guru, whose state is beyond knowing: the revered Ram Das is the boat that carries across. ॥4॥
1402.3: Those who have taken (the Guru's) word as unshakable, as Dhru did, are the beings saved from death.
They have crossed the terrible ocean in an instant; (to them) the world is made like the shadow of a cloud.
In the Sat Sangat the coiled knot (of their minds) has come undone, and through the Guru they glow with supreme bliss.
The revered Guru, the Master, is above all; let the True One be served in thought, word and deed. ॥5॥
1402.4: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved.
Lotus-eyed, sweet of speech, beautiful amid millions of companions, (you are the one) whom mother Jasod would urge: eat curd and rice, dear one.
Seeing your peerless beauty she was lost in love, when you played and the bells of your waistband jingled.
The pen of death and the command are in your hand: tell me, who can erase (them)? Shiva and Brahma long to hold your knowledge and meditation in their hearts.
You alone are ever the True, the Eternal, the abode of Lakshmi, the Primal Being: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved. ॥1॥
1402.5: Your name is Ram, your abode the highest; pure is your understanding; formless, beyond count: who can equal you?
Steady of mind, for your devotee's sake you took on a form (as Narasimha), and slew Harnakhash, tearing him open with your nails.
(Yours are) the conch, the discus, the mace and the lotus; you yourself took on a guise of guile; you are the infinite Paarbrahm (the Supreme Lord): who can know you?
You alone are ever the True, the Eternal, the abode of Lakshmi, the Primal Being: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved. ॥2॥
1402.6: Clad in yellow, your teeth white as the kund flower, your beloved beside you, a garland at your throat, you gladly wear on your head a crown of peacock feathers.
You need no minister; you are greatly patient, righteousness embodied, beyond knowing and beyond reach; you have staged this play for your own delight.
Your story is beyond telling and cannot be told; you pervade the three worlds; of your own will you have taken this form, O King of kings.
You alone are ever the True, the Eternal, the abode of Lakshmi, the Primal Being: Waheguru, Waheguru, Waheguru: wondrous are you, beloved. ॥3॥
1403.1: Gubind (the Lord of the universe) himself is the True Guru, the True Guru, the True Guru.

He is the deceiver of Bali, the crusher of the mighty, who makes devotion bear fruit, the prince Kanh (Krishna); he is Nihkalank (the stainless one to come), whose drum sounds, with whom the hosts of the sun and moon will march.
He is Ram, who pervades all, the destroyer of sins, who brings well-being to all the worlds; he himself is in all beings; he is the god of gods, and the thousand-mouthed king of serpents.
He took birth and did his deeds as the fish, the tortoise and the boar, and played the game of ball on the bank of the Jamuna.
O mind of Gayand, enshrine the sublime Name in your heart and give up vice: Gubind himself is the True Guru, the True Guru, the True Guru. ॥4॥
1403.2: The revered Guru, the revered Guru, the revered Guru is true for ever.
Accept what the Guru says as your own treasure, and know this mantra as true: night and day it brings well-being, and you will attain the supreme state.
Give up lust, anger, greed and attachment, and deceit towards everyone; cut the noose of Haumai (ego), and love the Saadh Sangat.
Body, home, love of a wife: this world is the play of the mind; ever serve (the Guru's) lotus feet, and make your understanding firm.
O mind of Gayand, enshrine the sublime Name in your heart and give up vice: the revered Guru, the revered Guru, the revered Guru is true for ever. ॥5॥
1403.3: Age after age you fill (the hearts of) your servants; O Waheguru, all is your blessing.
You are the Formless Lord, ever intact; no one can say since when you have been.
You created countless Brahmas and Vishnus; they fell into attachment to the pride of their own minds.
You brought forth the eighty-four lakh species, and since then have given sustenance to them all.
Age after age you fill (the hearts of) your servants; O Waheguru, all is your blessing. ॥1॥
1403.4: Vast is the play of the Wondrous One.
He himself laughs, he himself thinks; he himself gives light to the sun and the moon.
He is the water, he the land and what holds it up; he himself has made his dwelling in every heart.
He himself is man, and he himself woman; he himself is the piece, and he himself the dice.
O Sangat, all of you, reflect through the Guru: vast is the play of the Wondrous One. ॥2॥
1403.5: You have made this play, this great meeting (of the elements), this spectacle; O Waheguru, all creation is yours.
You pervade the water, the land, the sky and the netherworld; your words are sweeter than Amrit.
Brahma and the rest, Rudra (Shiva) and the rest, revere you; you are the death of death; O Immaculate One, (all) beg of you.
By the Guru's grace the highest good is obtained, and the mind is bound to the Sat Sangat.
You have made this play, this great meeting (of the elements), this spectacle; O Waheguru, all creation is yours. ॥3॥
1404.1: He who is beyond reach, endless and without beginning, whose beginning no one knows,
on whom Shiva and Biranchi (Brahma) meditate daily, whom the Veda describes,
formless and without enmity, with no second other than him,
able to break and to fashion, that God is the boat that carries across;
he who made the world in many forms, his servant Mathura savours with his tongue.
The revered True Name, the Creator, the all-pervading Being, dwells in the mind of Guru Ram Das. ॥1॥
1404.2: I have taken hold of the all-powerful Guru, to gain steady understanding and good counsel,
whose banner of righteousness ever flies; (I hold to him) to drive away the heaps and waves of sin.
Knowing it, his servant Mathura has spoken this truth from the heart, and there is nothing else to consider:
in the Kalyug, the great ship that ferries (us) over the world-ocean is the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
1404.3: Constantly, in the company of the Sat Sangat, dyed in a beautiful colour, they sing (the Lord's) praise.
The Sustainer of the earth has himself laid down the path of righteousness; they stay absorbed in him and do not wander.
Mathura says: good is their fortune, and they obtain the fruits their minds desire.
What fear of the son of the Sun can they have who fix their minds on the Guru's feet? ॥3॥
1404.4: (The Guru is a pool) brimming with the pure nectar of the Name; before daybreak the waves of the Shabad rise in it.
It is deep, profound, unfathomable and vast, ever brimming over, in every way a mine of jewels.
The Sants, like swans, delight in it; their fear of Jam and the record of their sorrows are wiped out.
To drive away the sins of the Kalyug, the sight of the Guru is an ocean of every peace. ॥4॥
1404.5: He on whom the sages meditate, wandering through all the ages, while only now and then does one find the inner light;
whose praise Biranchi sings with the words of the Vedas; holding to whom, Shiva the sage does not leave Kailash;
for whom countless yogis, celibates, Siddhas and seekers practise austerities, and wander about detached, in the guise of matted locks:
that True Guru, of his own gracious will, showed mercy to all beings, and gave Guru Ram Das the glory of the Name. ॥5॥
1404.6: (He has) the treasure of the Name; his meditation is turned within; the mass of his radiance shines through the three worlds.
Beholding his sight, doubt flees in confusion, sorrows are cast off, and the joys of Sahaj blossom.
His servants and Sikhs are ever drawn to him, as swarms of bees to the fragrance of a flower.
The Guru, while still present (in body), himself established the true throne of Guru Ram Das, firm for ever. ॥6॥
1405.1: He has carried across the world, entranced by the intoxication of Maya, giving it the all-powerful Amrit Name.
And he is glorious, ever rich in peace and wealth; riddhis and siddhis never leave his side.
He is a great giver, of boundless might: his servant and slave (Mathura) has told this truth.
Why should he care for anyone, on whose head the Guru has laid his hand? ॥7॥
1405.2: He alone pervades the three worlds;
he has made no one in the world like himself;
gods, men and demons have not found his end.
The gods, the demons, men, the ganas and the Gandharbs have not found his end, though they went searching.
He is imperishable, unmoving, beyond birth, self-existent, the highest Being, infinite and beyond all.
He alone is ever the cause of creation, all-powerful; all beings have meditated on him in their minds.
O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥1॥
1405.3: The True Guru Nanak worshipped with a single mind, and gave his body, mind and wealth to Gobind.
(Guru) Angad enshrined within himself the One of endless forms; with the knowledge of the Unreachable, his heart was steeped in love.
Guru Amar Das won the Creator over; he meditated on him, crying Wah, Wah.
O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥2॥
1405.4: Narad, Dhru, Prahlad and Sudama, who are counted the Lord's devotees of former ages;
Ambrik, Jaidev, Trilochan, Nama and Kabir too, who are named:
(of them, those) born in the Kalyug, their praise has spread over the whole world.
O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥3॥
1405.5: (O Guru,) those who remember you with the mind, their lust and anger are erased.
Those who remember you with speech, their pain and poverty are erased in an instant.
Those who touch your sight through their deeds become like the paaras; Bal the Bhatt has sung (your) praise.
O revered Guru Ram Das, the world hails your victory: you have attained the supreme state of the Lord. ॥4॥
1405.6: The True Guru, remembering whom the darkness of the eyes is gone in an instant;
remembering whom the Lord's Name (grows) in the heart day by day;
remembering whom one stills the burning within the soul;
remembering whom one obtains riddhis, siddhis and the nine treasures:
Bal says: that is Guru Ram Das; join the Sangat and call (him) blessed, blessed.
The True Guru, clinging to whom God is found: remember that True Guru, O people. ॥5॥
1405.7: He who lived the Shabad and attained the supreme state, and in his service never left (the Guru's) side:
from him the pearl of knowledge has shone forth, and its light destroys sorrow, poverty and darkness.
O poet Kirat, those who turn (from the world) and fall at the feet of that Sant have no fear of lust, anger or Jam.
As Angad was ever at Guru Nanak's side, so is Guru Ram Das with Guru Amar Das. ॥1॥
1406.1: He who served the True Guru and obtained the treasure (of the Name), who dwells night and day at the Lord's feet:
and so the whole vast Sangat honours you with love and reverence; you are the sandalwood of Malyagar, your fragrance spreading for all to know.
The light that welled up in Dhru, Prahlad, Kabir and Tilochan as they took the Name,
seeing which great joy fills the mind, is Guru Ram Das, the support of the Sants. ॥2॥
1406.2: (Guru) Nanak recognised the Name of the Immaculate One, and worshipped (him), fixing his attention in love.
From him came Angad, an ocean (of virtues), ever at his side; he laid the foundation of joining the attention to the Shabad.
The story of Guru Amar Das cannot be told: with one tongue nothing of it can be said.
Now, to carry the whole world across, the glory has come to Guru Ram Das, the Sodhi. ॥3॥
1406.3: We are full of faults, without a single virtue; leaving the Amrit, we have eaten poison, nothing but poison.
Fallen into attachment to Maya and into doubt, we have gone astray, and have given our love to sons and wife.
We have heard of one sublime path, the Guru's Sangat; joining it, the fear of Jam has been wiped out.
Kirat the Bhatt has one prayer: O Guru Ram Das, keep (me) in your refuge. ॥4॥
1406.4: (O Guru Ram Das,) you have crushed attachment and brought it under your sway; seizing lust by the hair, you have thrown it to the ground.
With your might you have cut anger to pieces, and driven greed away in disgrace.
Birth and death, with palms joined, obey whatever your command may be.
You have bound the world-ocean, and, well pleased, carried the Sikhs across.
Over your head is the royal canopy, and your throne is true; you are mighty, joining Jog and worldly enjoyment.
Sal speaks the truth: O Guru Ram Das, your rule is unshakable, and your army unbroken. ॥1॥
1406.5: In all four ages you are the True Guru; you yourself are the Supreme God.
From the very first, gods, men, seekers, Siddhas and Sikhs have been your servants.
You are from the beginning, from the start of the ages, without beginning; your power upholds the three worlds.
You are the saviour of the Agam and the Nigam; you ride upon old age and Jam.
Guru Amar Das has established you, firm for ever; you have gone across, and are the boat that carries (others) across.
The poet Sal heeds neither sin nor Death: O Guru Ram Das, (he is in) your refuge. ॥2॥
